resources.title: Operations Hub
resources.why: Open the main JP AEC Operations Hub landing page.
resources.how: Use this as the starting point before choosing Map, Site Operations, Workspace or Guide.

resources.title: Checklist for Today — personally authored
resources.why: Write your own tasks for today's project; no historical source questions auto-populate.
resources.how: Select a project, add checklist lines and copy them manually. Browser-local only, not saved to Drive.

resources.title: Control Towers & Main Library
resources.why: Find documented A9 version pointers and Main Library entry point from the website.
resources.how: Search the directory and open the actual Drive source. This is a dated snapshot until automatic sync is implemented.

resources.title: Operational Project Map
resources.why: See project identity, location, lifecycle and public portfolio context.
resources.how: Search/filter projects and open project/site-operations details from the map.

resources.title: JP AEC Guide
resources.why: Choose a 1-page, 3-page, 7-page or 15-page operating guide.
resources.how: Use the 1-page quick start for routine work; use deeper guides for training/reference. Print/Save PDF is built in.

resources.title: Pending Work Registry
resources.why: Keep prepared proposals and deferred implementation work visible so important follow-up is not lost between chat threads.
resources.how: Open this page before starting a new roadmap item; follow the proposal link and explicit next approval gate.

resources.title: Fishtail Materials & Daily Progress
resources.why: Human-readable downstream view for Fishtail material and Daily Ops records.
resources.how: Review or enter governed human data only in the intended tabs; do not treat a Sheet copy as independent project-master truth.

resources.title: Rohini Site Visit, Materials & Daily Progress
resources.why: Human-readable downstream view for Rohini site-visit and Daily Ops records.
resources.how: Use as a controlled input/projection surface; verify project identity before entering a fact.

resources.title: Daily Ops current state
resources.why: Machine-readable current operational truth for work, readiness, materials, blockers and evidence.
resources.how: Read this when debugging what the website currently believes; changes should be evidence-backed and paired with event history.

resources.title: Daily Ops append-only history
resources.why: Preserve how the current operational state changed over time.
resources.how: Use one event per line. Append supported facts/projections; do not rewrite history to make the present look cleaner.

resources.title: Project resource-link registry
resources.why: Connect project IDs to permission-gated engineering files without copying the actual documents into public GitHub.
resources.how: Drive owns the file; this JSON owns the normalized project-to-resource relationship.

resources.title: Project master · projects.csv
resources.why: Own project identity, lifecycle/status, coordinates and public project attributes.
resources.how: Edit by stable project ID. Do not maintain competing project-master facts in HTML or a downstream Sheet.

resources.title: Map configuration
resources.why: Own allowed map statuses and presentation configuration.
resources.how: Change labels/styles here rather than hardcoding duplicated values into page logic.

resources.title: Daily Ops PostgreSQL schema contract
resources.why: Define relational entities, primary keys, foreign keys and constraints for Daily Ops.
resources.how: Treat this as the relationship contract today. It does not mean a live Neon/PostgreSQL server is required.

resources.title: Live database connection
resources.why: Clarify whether this static site currently depends on a hosted PostgreSQL/Neon database.
resources.how: Current state: no live database is required by the Pages runtime. Introduce one only when authenticated multi-user transactional writes justify it.

resources.title: JP Scheduling, Work & Resource Management
resources.why: Own scheduling, sequencing, calendars, resources and project-specific execution planning.
resources.how: Use this module for Primavera/open-source scheduling work rather than putting scheduling logic inside Daily Ops.

resources.title: JP Cost Estimation
resources.why: Own estimation, BOQ and cost-engine development.
resources.how: Use the Operations Hub for project context and route cost-specific work to this specialist module.

resources.title: JP Structural Analysis
resources.why: Own OpenSees/SAR structural-analysis engine development and validated reporting.
resources.how: Use this module for structural computation/report generation; R&D research pages should link here rather than becoming the engine.

resources.title: JP Computer-Aided Drawings
resources.why: Own CAD/drawing publication and drawing-system development.
resources.how: Keep drawing production separate from Daily Ops while linking approved/current project resources back into project pages.

resources.title: JP Research & Development
resources.why: Publish the higher-level R&D hub containing AEC/Structural Research and Hydropower Research.
resources.how: Use for research dissemination; executable specialist products live in their own repositories.

resources.title: Operations Hub source repository
resources.why: Inspect source, version history, branches and governed changes.
resources.how: Normal Daily Ops development occurs on feature/daily-ops-current-work; main is not silently mutated.

resources.title: GitHub Actions
resources.why: Verify machine-data validation and Pages deployment.
resources.how: After a governed change, confirm the latest intended head finishes SUCCESS before calling the website current.

resources.title: Canonical Data Authority
resources.why: Explain which layer owns project masters, Daily Ops current state, history, files and projections.
resources.how: Read this before introducing a new storage system or moving truth into a Sheet/HTML page.

resources.title: Platform module boundaries
resources.why: Keep Operations, Scheduling, Cost, Structural and CAD responsibilities separated.
resources.how: Use it before adding a feature to decide which repository should own that capability.

resources.title: Workspace + Guide parity roadmap
resources.why: Track the five bounded phases from Workspace foundation through production release.
resources.how: Use this as the phase boundary/checklist; do not call later phases complete early.

resources.title: Branch / Lane Registry
resources.why: Resolve which Git branches are active working lanes, frozen archives or legacy aliases before any repository mutation.
resources.how: Read this before choosing a branch. Work only where allowed_for_work=true; never continue new work on a legacy alias or frozen archive.

resources.title: Pinned data routing & A9-CWO daily procedure
resources.why: Remember where raw communication, machine facts, control rules, libraries, images and website projections belong.
resources.how: Review storage matrix and daily steps before adopting any new provider.

resources.title: A9-CWO Memory Wall · pinned visual runbook
resources.why: Remind operators of no-overwrite, every-edit date enumeration, source archive and daily scan/readback.
resources.how: Open it daily, print/save for offline reference; follow links to live notebook and revision ledger.
resources.type: Printable job aid and cheat sheet

resources.title: Discord: two-channel daily Colab intake
resources.why: Save new field images and messages from exactly the two approved Discord channels before reconciliation.
resources.how: Run Colab using a Discord bot credential and authorized Google Drive account; verify PASS handoff receipt. Preview status means notebook code is staged, not that Discord was collected.

resources.title: Owner Workspace — project directory
resources.why: Find ownership, project links, source records and specialist modules in one resource directory.
resources.how: Use the project and drawing shortcuts at the top; select the right discipline.

resources.title: Drawings & Models — DWG / SKP / E2K / PDF
resources.why: Find all registered architectural, structural, CAD and engineering model originals by project and format.
resources.how: Choose a site, select the file format, and open the verified source pointer in Google Drive. Revisions are not automatically approved.

resources.title: Site Coordination — holds and engineering questions
resources.why: Review unresolved holds, pending decisions and engineer questions separately from daily personal tasks.
resources.how: Select the project, follow the original Slack/Discord source and obtain a responsible decision.

resources.title: Progress Report — source-attributed communication history
resources.why: Read staged, typed field-reported progress and preserved historic follow-ups.
resources.how: Select project, check Discord/Slack attribution, date and source; no work completion is inferred.
